body:
DELETE /account returns a 500 (sqlite3.IntegrityError: FOREIGN KEY constraint
failed) for any account that has ever minted an invite for a still-existing
list. accounts.delete_account() deletes auth_tokens, account_settings, and the
accounts row, but invites.created_by REFERENCES accounts(id) and those rows are
only removed when their list is GC-hard-deleted — so the final DELETE FROM
accounts is blocked. Reproduced against a fresh DB: register → create list →
mint invite → DELETE /account → 500.

Fix in accounts.delete_account(): delete the account's invite rows
(DELETE FROM invites WHERE created_by = ?) before deleting the account —
revoking a departed member's pending invites is also the right behavior
(otherwise an invite whose creator is gone would still admit the invitee).
Add a regression test (delete account after minting an invite; also after
minting an invite on a list that keeps other members).

Files: server/src/shoppinglist_server/accounts.py, server/tests/test_account.py.
title: Server: DELETE /account 500s (FK) once the account has minted an invite
